rubric.result: Walked the amended `### Desired end state` sentence by sentence against the accumulated diff. (1) 'For every new admission, the backend drives the existing plugin oracle after successful plan publication': `RunPlanAgents.launch` writes `run/admission.json` before the planner starts and hands the conversation to `#driveAfterPlanner`, which waits the planner, captures its measurements and runs `DriveRun`; `DriveRun.#drive` publishes only on the ABSENT path and then calls `machine.open`. `ct-api.ts` constructs `RunPlanAgents` as the one `planAgents` given to `#startPlan`, `startMilestonePlan`, `RecoverPlan`, `RequestFixes` and the review watcher, so loose and milestone admissions both route there with no parameter, variable, request field or alternate startup path. (2) 'The plugin alone chooses each step, retry, discard and terminal result': `CtRunMachine`/`OracleBoundary` parse only real `ct-step` stdout, import `STEPS` and `RUN_STATES`, never call `after`, query `next` again after an ordinary verb, and derive nothing from task or attempt numbers; a missing or malformed structured output installs JSON null and leaves the discard to the plugin's consumer. (3) 'Each supported model dispatch resumes the original conversation with the plugin's exact prepared files': `ClaudeRunCalls.#argv` is `-p --output-format stream-json --verbose --permission-mode acceptEdits --plugin-dir <root> --resume <conversation>` plus the role argv, and the errand lists `dispatch.paths` only, with the exact wrapper sentence the plan pinned; `RunDispatch.resolve` hashes every printed input and seals it as `material.json`, refusing changed bytes on replay. (4) 'The CLI receives the plugin's response schema and role tools. Judges use the plugin's agent definitions': `run-dispatch.ts` imports `REPORT_SCHEMA`, `VERDICT_SCHEMA`, `ADVICE_SCHEMA`, `SLICE_VERDICT_SCHEMA` for their matching roles, emits `--tools`/`--allowedTools` from `AgentDefinition.tools` checked against the plugin's own tool constants, and passes `--agents JSON.stringify(definition.toClaudeAgents())` with `--agent definition.name`; reconciliation returns edits with no invented schema. (5) 'Every call retains available CLI measurements. New projections omit unavailable metrics and label totals as reported totals': `ClaudeRunMeasurements.capture` writes `calls/<call>/measurements-v1.json` and is called for the planner, for every dispatched role call (including the judge), for fixes, and for completed history during explicit recovery; invalid or absent leaves are omitted with a diagnostic while measured zero survives, and `total_cost_usd` carries scope `initial-invocation` or `unverified-resume`, everything else `reported-only`. (6) 'Legacy call records remain readable. The backend writes no plugin attempt rows': `claude-calls.ts` gains only the `descriptorOf` delegation, no record schema moves, `CtRunMachine` only reads `.agent/run-<issue>.json` for before/after evidence, and no backend line writes an attempt row — `docs/superpowers/metrics/issue-332.jsonl` is this slice's own plugin-written telemetry. (7) 'Existing legacy records retain compatible recovery and fixes. Restart inspection preserves identity and never replays ambiguous operations': `RunPlanAgents.provenance` proves LEGACY only from one initial planner with a null request id plus one resumed outer implementation whose id is `implementation:<planner-id>` and no journal evidence, and delegates to the untouched adapters; `RunPlanRecovery.#recover` delegates the whole read to `RecordedPlanRecovery` when every record is positively legacy, and otherwise projects uncertain/inspect for unowned, forked, pending or identity-mismatched evidence while writing nothing and launching nothing. Every promise of the section is produced somewhere in the sum of the eleven task commits; none is absent and none is carried by a commit a later one undid.

Read `## Commits` in order (eleven #332 commits interleaved with merges of origin/main) against every `**Objective:**` of §7. The relationship between the commits is additive throughout: task 4 extends `ct-run-machine.ts` with `dispatch` and `run-journal.ts` with `material`/`seal`; task 7 extends the same two files with `admitted`/`admit`/`operationsPresent`, `descriptorOf` and the `unstarted` fact; task 8 adds `RunPlanAgents.owns`; task 9 wires the whole graph in `ct-api.ts`; no later commit removes or replaces what an earlier one established. I checked this the way a sum can be checked: every test title the plan names for tasks 1 through 10 — 52 titles across eleven files — is present in the final accumulated state (for example task 3's 'oracle exit nine survives the adapter unchanged' and task 7's 'untouched establishment differs from unrecorded machine activity' both survive task 7's later edit of `ct-run-machine.test.ts`), so no task's evidence was quietly retired by a successor. The one reversal in this slice is the plan amendment itself, and it is a declared closed decision of §2 ('The user later prohibited every feature flag or equivalent activation switch'): the flag it retired left no scaffolding behind — `CT_BACKEND_RUN_DRIVER`, a `runDriver` setting, a `'legacy' | 'machine'` mode and `run-driver-configuration.test.ts` appear nowhere in the tree, and `Invocation`, `Makefile` and `.env.example` carry no activation input, which is exactly what task 9's amended objective and its test 'existing entrypoints start without an activation setting' ask for. Nor do two tasks solve one problem twice: classification lives once in `RunPlanAgents.provenance` and task 8's `RunPlanRecovery` reuses it rather than parsing descriptors again, and the oracle's output is parsed once, in `OracleBoundary`.

Measured the `## Señal` cell against the accumulated diff and against `/Users/jponzvan/git/control-tower-plugin/.worktrees/370/plugin/conventions/simplicity.md`. Production code emits it: `backend/src/infrastructure/claude-run-measurements.ts` publishes `harness/<conversation>/calls/<call>/measurements-v1.json` carrying `version`, `conversation`, `callId`, `purpose`, `source` (stream and completion paths with their SHA-256 digests — the 'explicit source meaning' the cell promises), `reported`, `wallDurationMs` and `diagnostics`, and production callers reach it for every backend-owned model call: `claude-run-calls.ts:81` for each dispatched role including the judge, `run-plan-agents.ts:187` for the planner, `:276` for fixes and `:282` for completed history on explicit recovery. It lives in `src/`, not in a test or a fixture. With the repo's own instrumentation: it emits through `HeadlessFiles.writeOnce`, the same immutable-record primitive the existing per-call evidence already uses at `claude-calls.ts:660` and `headless-call-worker.ts:327` (`completion.json`), and the dependency manifest is untouched — `backend/package.json` and its lockfile change only the release version, no library arrives with this slice. Every label is bounded: the emission is a per-call immutable record whose identity is its own directory, not a dimension on a shared aggregate, so `conversation` and `callId` are the record's identity that the cell explicitly requires rather than a high-cardinality label fanning out a series; `purpose` is the closed three-value vocabulary, each projected value carries a scope from the closed set `initial-invocation`/`unverified-resume`/`reported-only`, and `reported.extra` keys are JSON pointers taken from the CLI's own output shape within that one call. No unbounded identifier is used as a metric dimension. The smell does not apply: the cell names an artifact read in production after the merge — `backend/API.md` says each completed call may add `measurements-v1.json` beside its stream and completion, and `docs/superpowers/evidence/issue-332-run-driver.md` names the reader and the action ('Monitor oracle refusals, pending or unresolved receipts, call diagnostics and each call's reported measurements. Do not sum reported totals as spend.') — which is also what `simplicity.md`'s 'who reads this, and where?' asks for. The cell's last clause holds too: the plugin tree is byte-identical to the pinned upstream, nothing in the diff appends a companion attempt row, and no historical telemetry is rewritten.
